after.worked_solution:
The denominator is $8-11\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $8+11\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $8+11\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12-19\text{i}}{8-11\text{i}} & =\frac{12-19\text{i}}{8-11\text{i}}\cdot \frac{8+11\text{i}}{8+11\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{(12-19\text{i})(8+11\text{i})}{(8-11\text{i})(8+11\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{96+132\text{i}-152\text{i}-209{\text{i}}^{2}}{{8}^{2}-(11\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{96-20\text{i}-209(-1)}{{8}^{2}+{11}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{96-20\text{i}+209}{64+121} \\  & =\frac{305-20\text{i}}{185} \\  & =\frac{5(61-4\text{i})}{5\cdot 37} \\  & =\frac{61-4\text{i}}{37}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{61-4\text{i}}{37}=(\frac{61}{37})+(-\frac{4}{37})\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{5+5\text{i}}{-3+8\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is $-3+8\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-3-8\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3-8\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{5+5\text{i}}{-3+8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5+5\text{i}}{-3+8\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-3-8\text{i}}{-3-8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-15-40\text{i}-15\text{i}-40{\text{i}}^{2}}{{3}^{2}-{8}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-15-55\text{i}-40(-1)}{{3}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-15-55\text{i}+40}{9+64} \\  & =\frac{25-55\text{i}}{73}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{25-55\text{i}}{73}=\frac{25}{73}-\frac{55}{73}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Multiply by the conjugate 6-3i. The numerator is (2-5i)(6-3i)=12-36i+15i²=-3-36i, and the denominator is 36+9=45. Dividing gives -1/15-(4/5)i, option b.

after.problem: If ${z}_{1}=2-5\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=6+3\text{i}$, then ${z}_{1}$ divided by ${z}_{2}$ equals
after.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{2-5\text{i}}{6+3\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is $6+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $6-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $6-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{2-5\text{i}}{6+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{2-5\text{i}}{6+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{6-3\text{i}}{6-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{12-6\text{i}-30\text{i}+15{\text{i}}^{2}}{{6}^{2}-{3}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12-36\text{i}+15(-1)}{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12-36\text{i}-15}{36+9} \\  & =\frac{-3-36\text{i}}{45}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-3-36\text{i}}{45}=-\frac{3}{45}-\frac{36}{45}\text{i}=-\frac{1}{15}-\frac{4}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
